scope: IMP-02 / R2 item: batch package-manager update with preview, skip semantics and failure retry
status: implemented-and-isolated-verified; no real manager was updated
gapClosed: ROADMAP R2 item previously recorded as unfinished: 批量更新、跳过与失败项重试均未实现

implementation.preview: preview_package_manager_updates returns every catalog manager's read-only preview plus ready/blocked splits; blocked managers keep their reason instead of being dropped
implementation.batchExecution: update_package_managers takes the exclusive guards once for the whole run, reuses the single-tool executor per manager, and never holds the lock per tool
implementation.skipSemantics: A refusal before any command runs (missing command, unsupported self-update, Yarn Berry, unverifiable pip interpreter, or an explicit user skip) is reported as skipped with its reason and is never counted as a failure
implementation.retry: retryable is derived from items whose outcome is failed, so the UI cannot drift from what actually happened; the retry dialog resends only those tools and merges results back without losing the first run
implementation.ui: A 批量更新 button opens a read-only preview listing each manager's current version, executable and exact command (or its skip reason); confirming runs only the ready tools; the result dialog labels every outcome and offers 重试失败项

defectsFixed: The single-tool command had to be split into guard + inner so a batch could hold the locks once; the first refactor returned the guards unbound, which would have dropped every lock immediately — caught and fixed before verification.
The batch result dialog initially stacked on top of the still-open preview; the preview is now closed when the batch completes.

notVerified: No real package manager was updated; every execution went through the UI fixture
Batch behaviour under a real mid-run failure (disk full, locked binary) was not exercised
Only one updatable manager plus one blocked manager were modelled in the fixture, not all ten at once
limitations: Managers run sequentially; there is no progress indicator between tools, only the final per-tool report
A batch never retries automatically: the user must confirm the retry
Target versions remain unknowable before execution, so the preview shows the current version and command only
